reports.title: Changing Weather for Late Fall Fishermen
reports.text:
Both crappie and bass anglers took advantage of it too by heading to the lake and soaking up the last of November’s sunny offering.
Decent stringers of crappie have been taken recently by anglers targeting manmade fish attractors such as brushpiles and stake beds in the 8 to 13 foot depth range. A few scattered crappie were caught recently in some shallow structure around the 4 to 8 foot depth range in West Sandy and up Big Sandy.
As always there are boats stalking the main lake ledges in deeper water at times and finding some crappie holding on the deep side of drop-offs in 13 to 17 foot depths.
No doubt the bass fishing will fall victim to the changing weather as well.
Scattered reports…

reports.title: Scott McGlinchey's Fishing Report
reports.text:
As water temperatures continue to cool, the bass fishing on Kentucky Lake has really improved. We're now catching more quality bass, and it's becoming increasingly common to catch bigger fish than smaller ones.
The topwater bass bite started in late July and has continued right through the summer and into the fall. During August and early September, we caught good numbers of bass, with several different locations producing schooling fish on and off throughout the day.
